title: Analysis iron distribution methods in fine sand- and silt-sized soil particles
author: He, Li, et al.

steps.title: Collect EDS spectra
steps.instruction: Acquire an EDS spectrum for each individual sand‑ or silt‑sized particle using the SEM‑EDS system.

steps.title: Identify minerals by library match
steps.instruction: Automatically compare each particle’s spectrum to the standard patterns in the mineral library and assign a mineral identity when the similarity exceeds a high threshold value.

steps.title: Handle unknown spectra
steps.instruction: If a spectrum does not match any library pattern, label the particle as “unknown”; re‑collect its EDS spectrum with the MLA processing tool, inspect it manually, and classify clay‑aggregate particles, which are then excluded from the final modal mineral abundance.

steps.title: Map complex particles
steps.instruction: For particles containing multiple mineral phases, generate a digital image pixel‑by‑pixel using thousands of X‑ray measurements via the MLA processing tool (single‑particle mapping).

steps.title: Segment phases in BSE image
steps.instruction: Create a phase‑segmented BSE image for each complex particle by assigning a unique color to regions of homogeneous gray level, which correspond to individual mineral phases.

steps.title: Calculate area‑based percentages
steps.instruction: Determine the area of each phase (simple or complex) and compute area‑based percentages of the sample’s mineral components.

steps.title: Convert to weight percentages
steps.instruction: Convert the area‑based percentages to weight percentages using the known mineral densities; report these values as the modal mineral abundances.

steps.title: Obtain iron concentrations
steps.instruction: Retrieve the iron concentration (k_i) for each silicate mineral phase from EMPA data (Supplementary Table 1S).

steps.title: Compute phase iron content
steps.instruction: Multiply the iron concentration (k_i) by the weight percentage of the mineral phase (C_i) to obtain the iron content of the phase (F_i).

steps.title: Calculate total silicate iron
steps.instruction: Sum the iron contents (F_i) of all identified silicate phases containing iron to obtain the total silicate‑bearing iron (F_sili).

steps.title: Determine iron partitioning
steps.instruction: For each silicate phase, divide its iron content (F_i) by the total silicate iron (F_sili) and multiply by 100 % to obtain the relative iron partition (P_i).

description: The chemical concentration, specifically the iron concentration, in each of the silicate mineral phases is obtained from the EMPA measured data [11]. Note that the data template is listed in Supplementary Table 1S. The iron concentration of each silicate mineral phase is multiplied by its modal abundance (Supplementary Table 2S), which is determined by Eq. (1). The total iron content in all the identified silicate phases containing iron is calculated using Eq. (2). As a percentage of the total silicate-bearing iron content, the iron content in one specific silicate mineral was used as its iron partition (%), which is expressed by Eq. (3). Here, we use the relative iron partition (%) for each of the identified silicate phases containing iron as the best approximate estimation of iron speciation (Supplementary Table 2S). Thus, the quantitative iron speciation is determined using Eq. (3). For greater simplification, the parameters in these equations use abbreviations, wherein ki is the iron concentration in mineral phase i, Ci is the weight percentage of mineral phase i, Fi is the weight percentage of the iron content in mineral phase i in the total mass, Fsili is the total iron content in all identified silicate phases containing iron, and Pi is the relative percentage of iron content in mineral phase i versus the total iron content in all identified silicate phases containing iron.(1)Fi=ki*Ci,(2)Fsili=∑i=1nki*Ci,(3)Pi=Fi/Fsili*100%,
